newsitem.title: INDIA: NEW INDIA BOND CUT-OFF AT 11.23-11.29 PCT - I-SEC.
newsitem.headline: NEW INDIA BOND CUT-OFF AT 11.23-11.29 PCT - I-SEC.

text.p: The cut-off yield on a eight-year bond due to be auctioned on Monday evening is likely to between 11.23 percent and 11.29 percent, ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said in a report on Monday.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) auctions federal government eight-year bonds worth 30 billion rupees later today.
I-Sec recommended the following bidding pattern:
I-Sec said the RBI had drained over 130 billion rupes from the banking system in the last 25 days, through issues of 364-day treasury bills and bonds.
Given these factors, the bidding interest is unlikely to be of the order seen at recent auctions, it said.
I-Sec said trading volumes in government securities have been failry large over the past few weeks, averaging more than 7.5 billion rupees daily.

"Importantly, 60 percent or more of these trades have been in securities with a residual maturity of over five years," it said. "Clearly the interest in longer-dated bonds is much higher than in short-dated ones."
I-Sec said while it is unlikely that the new bond will gain much in the short-term, holding period returns over two to three weeks could be excellent.
"About 52 billion rupees of the 13.50 percent 1997, maturing on September 1, is held by the market."
"If the gilt auction expected to coincide with the redemption of this security is anything less than 50 billion rupees, it would imply a significant inflow for the banking system," I-Sec said.
This could result in a surge in security prices, particularly at the long end, it said.
I-Sec is the Indian arm of investment bank J.P.Morgan.
